subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Drag Racing: The Quarter Mile
description: Learn Drag Racing: The Quarter Mile in one minute.

hook.text: Drag racing distills speed into its purest form—two cars, a straight line, a quarter mile.

buildup.text: Top Fuel dragsters produce over 11,000 horsepower and cover the strip in under 3.7 seconds.

discovery.text: The engine burns 15 gallons of nitromethane per run—roughly one gallon per second of racing.

twist.text: After each run, the engine is completely rebuilt because the extreme forces destroy it every time.

climax.text: Top speeds exceed 330 mph, making dragsters faster than any other wheeled vehicle on the planet.

punchline.text: The fastest cars on Earth are destroyed after every race.

quiz.question: How long does a Top Fuel dragster take to cover a quarter mile?

details.summary: Drag racing is a straight-line acceleration contest over a quarter mile, where purpose-built Top Fuel dragsters reach over 330 mph in under 3.7 seconds, producing over 11,000 horsepower.
details.whyItMatters: Drag racing distills motorsport to pure acceleration. Its technology pushes the limits of tire grip, fuel chemistry, and engine power in ways that advance performance understanding.
takeaways: Top Fuel dragsters cover the quarter mile in under 3.7 seconds
They produce over 11,000 horsepower from supercharged V8 engines
Drivers experience over 5 Gs of acceleration force at launch

faq.question: How can drag racing tires grip the track at such extreme power?
faq.answer: Drag slicks are made from extremely soft rubber compounds that deform and wrap around the track surface. The track is coated with a sticky rubber compound called VHT that dramatically increases grip.

faq.question: How often do drag racing engines need rebuilding?
faq.answer: Top Fuel engines are completely torn down and rebuilt between every run. Each pass generates such extreme forces that pistons, rods, and bearings are replaced after every quarter-mile blast.
